summary: A cleaned CSV of 1.5M+ US 501(c)(3) and 501(c) nonprofit organizations sourced from the IRS Exempt Organization Business Master File (BMF) and ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer — fully public, no authentication required. Fields include organization name, EIN, address (city, state, ZIP), NTEE mission code (education, health, arts, religion, environment, etc.), total revenue, total assets, gross receipts, form type (990/990-EZ/990-PF), and filing year. Candid (formerly GuideStar) charges $2,000–$9,500/year for essentially the same underlying data, Dataro charges $500+/month for nonprofit prospect lists, and GrantStation charges $200/month for grant and nonprofit directories. A $59 one-time Gumroad flat file undercuts every incumbent by 95%+ and serves grant writers, nonprofit SaaS vendors, corporate sponsorship teams, and accounting firms that need a bulk list of US nonprofits but cannot justify enterprise subscriptions.

audience.who: Nonprofit grant writing consultants and freelancers who need prospect lists of foundations and peer organizations; nonprofit SaaS vendors (Bloomerang, Blackbaud, Salesforce NPSP, Virtuous) whose SDRs need bulk lists of mid-size nonprofits ($500K–$5M revenue) to prospect; corporate social responsibility and sponsorship teams filtering nonprofits by mission type and geography; accounting and audit firms targeting nonprofit audit clients by size; healthcare consultants analyzing the nonprofit health-system market (hospitals, FQHCs, clinics that file 990s).

data_wanted: IRS Exempt Organization Business Master File (BMF) — the IRS publishes this monthly as a free download at https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/exempt-organizations-business-master-file-extract-eo-bmf. Fields per record: organization name, EIN, street address, city, state, ZIP, NTEE code (3-character mission classification), subsection code (501c type), affiliation, classification, ruling year, deductibility, foundation code, activity codes, organization code, status, tax period, asset code, income code, filing requirement, PF filing requirement, accounting period, asset amount, income amount, form 990 revenue. For enrichment: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API (https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/api/v2/) provides total revenue, total expenses, and officer data per EIN with no API key required. No login or authentication required for either source.

evidence.source: Candid (formerly GuideStar) — the dominant nonprofit data platform, charges $2,000–$9,500/year for nonprofit search and export access, all built on the same IRS public filing data
evidence.quote: Candid's GuideStar database includes millions of IRS-recognized nonprofits. Premium access starts at $2,000/year for Seals of Transparency and data export features.

evidence.source: Dataro — nonprofit AI prospect research platform charging $500+/month; explicitly positions against the need to purchase nonprofit bulk lists for donor acquisition modeling
evidence.quote: There are approximately 1.8 million nonprofit organizations in the United States. Over 1.5 million are registered with the IRS as tax-exempt organizations.

evidence.source: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer — free API and search tool proving the data is public; 1.8M+ nonprofit returns searchable by name, state, EIN, and revenue
evidence.quote: Nonprofit Explorer provides summaries and PDFs of 990 documents for 1.8+ million tax-exempt organizations, all sourced from IRS public data. The API provides programmatic access with no key required.

evidence.source: IRS Exempt Organization BMF — official monthly flat-file publication of all tax-exempt organizations, no authentication required
evidence.quote: The Exempt Organizations Business Master File Extract provides information about organizations that have been recognized by the IRS as tax-exempt under subsections of Internal Revenue Code section 501.

willingness_to_pay.signal: The nonprofit data market is mature and enterprise-priced: Candid runs $2K–$9.5K/year, Foundation Directory Online (FDO) is $1,200+/year, DonorSearch and iWave run $500–$3,000/month for prospect research, and GrantStation charges $200/month. The long tail of solo grant writers, small nonprofit consultants, and early-stage SaaS SDR teams cannot afford these platforms. A $59 flat CSV with 1.5M+ organizations, NTEE mission codes, and revenue tiers is a decisive price-point win. Bonus segment: accounting firms prospecting for nonprofit audit clients — a $59 spend to identify 50 target nonprofits in their state is trivially justified at audit fee rates of $5K–$25K per engagement.

first_sale_path.channel: Gumroad one-time download + LinkedIn posts targeting nonprofit consultants, grant writers, and nonprofit SaaS founders + r/nonprofit and r/grantwriting subreddit contextual posts + direct LinkedIn outreach to Blackbaud/Bloomerang SDRs and solo grant writing consultants
first_sale_path.angle: Title: 'US Nonprofit Database 2026 — 1.5M+ IRS Tax-Exempt Organizations with Revenue, NTEE Codes & Addresses (CSV)'. Key selling points: (1) Same source as Candid/GuideStar — the IRS BMF, updated monthly, (2) NTEE mission codes included — filter by education, health, arts, environment, religion in seconds, (3) Revenue and asset tiers — identify mid-size $500K–$5M nonprofits in your state for SaaS prospecting or audit targeting, (4) One-time $59 — not $2,000/year. Primary grant writer angle: 'Find every 501(c)(3) in your state by mission type — 1.5M organizations, instant download, no subscription.'

ceo_decision.notes: Highest score (9), IRS BMF direct download, massive 1.5M+ record dataset, decisive market angle vs Candid $2K+/yr
